sections.h2: Why does a Louisville home sale go through the Jefferson County Clerk?
sections.html:
The Legal Records Division of the Jefferson County Clerk's office is the official repository for deeds, mortgages, releases and liens on Louisville real estate. Until your deed is taxed, accepted and indexed there, the sale does not show on the public record.

The Deed Room works out of Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204, Louisville, KY 40202, and its listed telephone is 502-574-6220. Wills and name changes pass through that same room after the probate court signs off, which helps if you inherited the house. Tax collection after April 15 sits at a different counter, Suite 100a in the same building.

The office runs a free alert service called ClerkAlert. It emails owners whenever a paper is filed under their name or business name, and some sellers keep it switched on after closing as a guard against forged deeds or surprise liens.

sections.h2: What does the Clerk charge to record a deed in Louisville?
sections.html:
A deed costs $50 and a mortgage costs $80. The clerk lists the full price list under KRS 64.012, as amended by Senate Bill 114, and the sample below is copied from that list.

Recording prices posted by the Jefferson County Clerk for common real estate papers (source: Jefferson County Clerk, Document Fees page)
Paper filedPrice
Deed$50
Deed filed together with a release$96
Deed that reserves a vendor's lien$50
Mortgage$80
Mortgage that includes an assignment$126
Stand-alone release$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$50

Several add-ons can raise the bill:

  • Instruments sent through the mail pick up a $1 postage charge starting September 1, 2026.
  • Certified copies cost $5 for three pages, then 50 cents a page.
  • Each extra book or reference tied to a document adds $4.
  • The clerk's in-house notary charges $2 per signature.

sections.h2: How does the state transfer tax work on a Jefferson County deed?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. KRS 142.050 taxes the grantor named in the deed at 50 cents for each $500 of declared value, rounding any leftover amount up to the next $500, and the clerk collects before recording.

Run the numbers for a house worth $248,400, the Census figure for a typical owned home here. That value holds 497 units of $500 after rounding up, so the tax is $248.50. Look for that charge on your settlement statement as its own line, apart from the recording fee.

Some transfers pay nothing. The ones sellers meet most often are these:

  • Husband and wife, or ex-spouses in a divorce.
  • A deed that only secures or releases a debt.
  • A corrective deed that confirms one already on record.
  • A foreclosure sale, or a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, when only nominal money changes hands.

The Clerk's checklist asks that a deed claiming exemption name the statute behind it.

sections.h2: What makes the Clerk turn a deed away?
sections.html:
Papers that miss the formatting or content checklist are returned at the counter. The checklist borrows the PRIA national layout standards that the Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted for filings from 2020 onward.

  • White letter-size paper, printed one side, with no staples, binding, embossed seals or highlighter.
  • Ten-point Times New Roman or a close match, black ink, and a three-inch blank band atop page one.
  • A preparation statement signed by whoever prepared the document. A "Drafted by" line does not count.
  • Full addresses for both parties, and a mailing address for future tax bills.
  • A legal description, the deed or will book and page of the seller's title, and a stated fair market value.
  • A notary block showing the notary's ID number and naming grantor and grantee.
  • An original or certified copy with the right fee in a signed check.

If the seller is a corporation, LLC or partnership, the Secretary of State must have the entity on file before the clerk will take its deed. Settle that point a week or two before the closing date.

sections.h2: How are mortgage payoffs recorded in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
Your lender files a release at $46 after the payoff clears. When a deed and a release travel together, the posted price for the pair is $96.

The Clerk's guidance reminds filers that a mortgage is recorded where the land sits, per KRS 382.110, and that it binds third parties from the moment it is acknowledged and recorded under KRS 382.080. The release must cite the book and page of the mortgage it wipes out, and the closing agent usually gets that from the title search.

Request a payoff letter that stays good through the closing date. Afterward, ask the title company when the release went out. A mortgage that stays open on the Jefferson County record can complicate the next owner's loan.

sections.h2: How does unpaid property tax reach the Clerk?
sections.html:
At the close of business on April 15, any current-year bill still open leaves the Sheriff and lands with the Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. By then the Sheriff's schedule has added a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent add-on fee, and the Clerk's side starts adding interest at 1 percent per month.

The County Attorney's tax page puts the combined extra cost near 40 percent once a certificate exists, and says certificates accrue interest at 12 percent a year. Each summer the Clerk holds a lien sale, and bills that fail to sell stay open for purchase all year. A buyer of a certificate can pile its own charges on top.

If nobody has bought the certificate, pay the Clerk at 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 100. Mailed payments must be certified or cashier's checks or money orders, because the office rejects personal checks and phone payments. A bill placed on a County Attorney payment plan cannot be sold at the sale.

Sellers should order a payoff figure before the listing goes live. Then the buyer's title company can settle it out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: What do sellers need to know about Jefferson County itself?
sections.html:
Kentucky's largest county covers 380.8 square miles of land along the Ohio River, and since the 2003 merger its lines match those of Louisville, the county seat. Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Middletown and dozens of smaller cities still keep their own governments inside Louisville Metro.

Public schools come from Jefferson County Public Schools and the Anchorage Independent district, which stops at eighth grade. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 795,222 residents in the 2025 estimate, up 1.6 percent from the April 2020 base.
  • 366,702 housing units counted in 2025.
  • 62.1 percent of households own their home (2020 to 2024).
  • $248,400 as the typical owned-home value.
  • $1,149 as median gross rent.
  • $69,866 as median household income.
  • 3,001 building permits issued during 2025.

The PVA's count of 83 taxing jurisdictions includes about 60,000 properties in the smaller home rule cities, many of which send their own bill. Recording works the same across all of them, but a seller in a small city should check for a city tax balance before closing.

faqs.q: Which office takes a deed for a house in Louisville?
faqs.a: The Jefferson County Clerk's Legal Records Division, in the Deed Room at Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204. Phone 502-574-6220. The closing agent normally files for the buyer, and the office also takes electronic filings.

faqs.q: What will I pay to put a deed on record?
faqs.a: The posted rate is $50 for a deed and $96 when a release is filed with it. Mailed instruments add $1 for postage from September 1, 2026, and the separate transfer tax runs 50 cents per $500 of value.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax charged to me or to the buyer?
faqs.a: Charged to you as grantor. KRS 142.050 imposes it on the seller named in the deed. Transfers such as those between spouses or through foreclosure are exempt when the deed cites the exemption.

faqs.q: Why would the Clerk reject my paperwork?
faqs.a: Typical causes are a missing preparation statement, no source of title, no stated market value, no tax-bill mailing address, a weak notary block or the wrong fee. An LLC seller also has to be registered with the Secretary of State first.

faqs.q: I owe back tax on the house. Where do I start?
faqs.a: Ask the Sheriff for any current-year balance before April 15, and the Clerk for older certificates afterward. Get both figures in writing before listing so the title company can pay them at closing. The County Attorney's Tax Division handles payment plans.
